Algebra I · Lesson 5.4

Systems in Disguise

Solve this lesson →All lessons

The choice between substitution and elimination comes down to coefficients, and a coefficient is only readable once an equation is written ax+by=cax+by=c. Plenty of systems are not written that way. Every system in this lesson is an ordinary one after a cleanup move from 4.4, and the new fact is that each of the two equations is cleaned on its own.

Problem
Eliminating yy from 6(x−2y)+7y=296(x−2y)+7y=29 and 4x+9y=1554x+9y=155 means comparing the two coefficients of yy. In the second equation that coefficient is 99. Enter the coefficient of yy in the first equation, once its left side is written as ax+byax+by.
Show a hint
  • To eliminate yy you compare the two coefficients of yy, and that coefficient is whatever multiplies yy once the left side is collected into one xx-term and one yy-term.
  • Distribute the 66 over x−2yx−2y to get 6x−12y6x−12y, then combine that with the +7y+7y outside the parentheses.
Show the full solution
Distributing gives 6x−12y+7y6x−12y+7y, and −12y+7y=−5y−12y+7y=−5y, so the left side is 6x−5y6x−5y and the coefficient of yy is −5−5​. The printed 77 is not the coefficient on its own, since distributing the 66 produces a second yy-term, −12y−12y, that combines with it.
Problem
Distributing and combining like terms turns 6(x−2y)+7y=296(x−2y)+7y=29 into 6x−5y=296x−5y=29, so the system is 6x−5y=296x−5y=29 and 4x+9y=1554x+9y=155. Eliminate xx the 5.3 way, back-substitute, and enter xx.
Show a hint
  • Nothing about elimination changes now that both equations are in ax+by=cax+by=c form. Compare the two coefficients on xx before scaling anything.
  • The xx-coefficients 66 and 44 both divide 1212, so double the first equation and triple the second.
Show the full solution
Doubling the first equation gives 12x−10y=5812x−10y=58 and tripling the second gives 12x+27y=46512x+27y=465. Subtracting the first of those from the second leaves 37y=40737y=407, so y=11y=11, and then 6x−55=296x−55=29 gives 6x=846x=84 and x=14x=14​. Check, 6(14)−5(11)=84−55=296(14)−5(11)=84−55=29 and 4(14)+9(11)=56+99=1554(14)+9(11)=56+99=155. Only the cleanup was new. Once both equations are in ax+by=cax+by=c form, elimination is the same work as in 5.3.
Key idea
Clean each side first. Distributing, from 2.1, and combining like terms, from 2.4, rewrite one side of an equation as an equal expression, so the new equation is true for exactly the same pairs as the old one, and the other equation of the system is untouched. A coefficient is the number multiplying a letter once that collecting is done, so the 77 printed in 6(x−2y)+7y6(x−2y)+7y is not the coefficient of yy. Until both letter terms are collected there is nothing to compare and no letter to isolate.
Problem
Neither equation of 4(x+3y)−5y=1234(x+3y)−5y=123 and 6x−3(y−4)=756x−3(y−4)=75 is in ax+by=cax+by=c form yet. Clean each one, solve the system, and enter the product xyxy. In the second equation the factor in front of the parentheses is −3−3, and it reaches both terms inside, signs included.
Show a hint
  • Expand and combine on the left of each equation the 2.1 way before a solving method is picked. The constant that comes out of the second expansion belongs on the right side with the 7575.
  • −3(y−4)−3(y−4) is −3y+12−3y+12, not −3y−12−3y−12, so the second equation cleans to 6x−3y=636x−3y=63 and then 2x−y=212x−y=21. Isolating yy there costs one move.
Show the full solution
Distributing gives 4x+12y−5y=1234x+12y−5y=123, so 4x+7y=1234x+7y=123, and 6x−3y+12=756x−3y+12=75, so 6x−3y=636x−3y=63 and 2x−y=212x−y=21. Then y=2x−21y=2x−21, and 4x+7(2x−21)=1234x+7(2x−21)=123 gives 18x=27018x=270, x=15x=15, y=9y=9, and xy=135xy=135​. The −3−3 reaches the −4−4 as well, which is why the constant lands as +12+12.
Problem
Neither 9x−33=3y+1329x−33=3y+132 nor 4y+5x=2x+204y+5x=2x+20 reads ax+by=cax+by=c, since one has a number on the left and each has letter terms on both sides. Use 4.3's balance moves on each, then solve the cleaned system and enter yy.
Show a hint
  • Take one equation at a time. Move every letter term to the left side and every number to the right side, doing the same thing to both sides at each step.
  • The first equation collects to 9x−3y=1659x−3y=165, and dividing both sides by 33 gives 3x−y=553x−y=55. The second collects to 3x+4y=203x+4y=20, so the xx-columns match.
Show the full solution
Collecting the first equation gives 9x−3y=1659x−3y=165, and dividing both sides by 33 gives 3x−y=553x−y=55. The second collects to 3x+4y=203x+4y=20. Subtracting the cleaned first equation from the cleaned second leaves 5y=−355y=−35, so y=−7y=−7​, with 3x=55−7=483x=55−7=48 and x=16x=16. Check (16,−7)(16,−7) in both originals, 144−33=111=−21+132144−33=111=−21+132 and −28+80=52=32+20−28+80=52=32+20. Once both equations read ax+by=cax+by=c, one subtraction finished the system.
Key idea
Standard form is ax+by=cax+by=c. Both letter terms on the left, the number alone on the right. 4.3's balance moves put any linear equation into that form by adding or subtracting the same thing on both sides. Two equations in that form can be stacked so the xx-terms share a column and the yy-terms share another, which is what 5.3 subtracts, and a coefficient of 11 is easy to spot, which is what 5.2 isolates without dividing. Both equations have to be in that form before there is anything to compare.
Problem
Clean 7x+4y=2x+3y+867x+4y=2x+3y+86 and 4(x+2y)−x−3y=1444(x+2y)−x−3y=144 into ax+by=cax+by=c form. Exactly one of the two letters can then be isolated with no division at all. Enter the value of that letter.
Show a hint
  • Nothing can be compared until both equations are in ax+by=cax+by=c form. Combine like terms in the first, and distribute the 44 in the second.
  • The cleaned system is 5x+y=865x+y=86 and 3x+5y=1443x+5y=144. Scan its four coefficients for a 11.
Show the full solution
Combining like terms in the first equation gives 5x+y=865x+y=86, and distributing in the second gives 4x+8y−x−3y=1444x+8y−x−3y=144, so 3x+5y=1443x+5y=144. The only coefficient of 11 is on the yy of the first equation, so y=86−5xy=86−5x, and 3x+5(86−5x)=1443x+5(86−5x)=144 becomes 430−22x=144430−22x=144, so 22x=28622x=286 and x=13x=13. Then y=86−65=21y=86−65=21​. Eliminating yy means scaling one equation to 5y5y, and eliminating xx means scaling both to 15x15x, so yy is the cheap letter either way.

4.4 cleared a fractional equation by multiplying both sides by a common denominator of its fractions, and one well-chosen multiplication removed every fraction at once. A system has two equations to run that on. The next two problems put fractions in one equation, then in both.

Problem
Solve x3+y2=173x​+2y​=17 and 4x−3y=604x−3y=60. Only one of the two equations has fractions in it, and the other already reads ax+by=cax+by=c. Enter xx.
Show a hint
  • The second equation has no fractions in it, so it needs no multiplier at all. Leave it as it is and work on the first.
  • The denominators 33 and 22 both divide 66. Multiply every term of the first equation by 66, the 1717 included.
Show the full solution
Multiplying the first equation by 66 gives 2x+3y=1022x+3y=102, and adding 4x−3y=604x−3y=60 leaves 6x=1626x=162, so x=27x=27​, with 3y=102−54=483y=102−54=48 and y=16y=16. Check, 9+8=179+8=17 and 108−48=60108−48=60. Each equation is cleaned on its own, so only the fractional one is multiplied.
Problem
Solve x10+y3=1510x​+3y​=15 and x9+y2=199x​+2y​=19. Each equation has its own pair of denominators, so clear the fractions one equation at a time. Enter xx.
Show a hint
  • Clearing the first equation takes a multiple of 1010 and 33. Clearing the second takes a multiple of 99 and 22. Choose the two multipliers separately.
  • Multiply the first equation by 3030 and the second by 1818, every term on both sides.
Show the full solution
Multiplying the first equation by 3030 gives 3x+10y=4503x+10y=450, and multiplying the second by 1818 gives 2x+9y=3422x+9y=342. Doubling the first result gives 6x+20y=9006x+20y=900, tripling the second gives 6x+27y=10266x+27y=1026, and subtracting leaves 7y=1267y=126, so y=18y=18. Then 3x+180=4503x+180=450 gives 3x=2703x=270 and x=90x=90​. The multiplier for each equation is built from that equation's own denominators, so the two multipliers are different.
Key idea
Each equation gets its own multiplier. The multiplier for an equation is a common denominator of the fractions in that equation, and every term on both sides of that equation is multiplied by it. Nothing about the other equation affects that choice, so the two multipliers are usually different numbers, 3030 for one and 1818 for the other. In 4.4 there was a single equation to clear, so one multiplier was the whole job. A system has two, and each is cleared on its own.
Problem
A student clears x3+4=y93x​+4=9y​ by multiplying by 99 and gets 3x+4=y3x+4=y. Paired with 5x+y=1245x+y=124 that line gives (15,49)(15,49), and the check fails, since 153+4=9315​+4=9 while 499949​ is not 99. Redo the clearing and enter the correct yy.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying by 99 has to multiply every term, and the first equation has three terms, not two.
  • The +4+4 sits on the same side as x33x​, so it gets multiplied as well and becomes 3636.
Show the full solution
Multiplying every term by 99 gives 3x+36=y3x+36=y. Substituting into 5x+y=1245x+y=124 gives 5x+3x+36=1245x+3x+36=124, so 8x=888x=88, x=11x=11, and y=3(11)+36=69y=3(11)+36=69​. Check, 113+4=233311​+4=323​ and 699=233969​=323​. Every term means the +4+4 as well, so 3x+4=y3x+4=y is a different equation, and the pair it gives fails the original.

A decimal coefficient is a count of tenths or hundredths, so a decimal equation is really a fraction equation, and one multiplication clears it just as before. The power of ten still comes from one equation at a time, so the two multipliers need not match.

Problem
Solve 0.6x+0.4y=370.6x+0.4y=37 and 0.07x−0.05y=1.90.07x−0.05y=1.9. The power of ten that clears an equation comes from the finest decimal place in that equation. Enter xx.
Show a hint
  • The first equation has nothing finer than tenths, and the second has hundredths, so the two powers of ten are not the same.
  • Multiply the first equation by 1010 and the second by 100100, both sides each time. The right sides then read 370370 and 190190.
Show the full solution
Clearing gives 6x+4y=3706x+4y=370 and 7x−5y=1907x−5y=190. Scaling to 20y20y and −20y−20y gives 30x+20y=185030x+20y=1850 and 28x−20y=76028x−20y=760, and adding leaves 58x=261058x=2610, so x=45x=45​, with y=25y=25. Check, 27+10=3727+10=37 and 3.15−1.25=1.93.15−1.25=1.9. Multiplying the second equation by 1010 would leave 0.7x0.7x and 0.5y0.5y behind.
Fun fact
In 1585 the Flemish engineer Simon Stevin published De Thiende, a pamphlet of a few pages that introduced decimal fractions to Europe and argued that every fraction should be written in tenths.

One shape from 4.4 is worth naming again. A fraction bar is a grouping symbol, so a numerator with two terms is grouped as a whole and needs parentheses the moment it is multiplied. Inside a system that numerator carries two letters instead of one, and that is the only difference from 4.4.

Problem
Solve 4x−y5=x+2y454x−y​=4x+2y​ and x+y=125x+y=125. Each side of the first equation is a single fraction and nothing else, so two multiplications clear it. Enter xx.
Show a hint
  • This is 4.4's shape with two letters in each numerator instead of one. The fraction bar groups its whole numerator.
  • Multiplying by 44 and then by 55 leaves 4(4x−y)=5(x+2y)4(4x−y)=5(x+2y). Collect that into ax+by=cax+by=c before using x+y=125x+y=125.
Show the full solution
Multiplying by 44 and then by 55 gives 4(4x−y)=5(x+2y)4(4x−y)=5(x+2y), so 16x−4y=5x+10y16x−4y=5x+10y and 11x=14y11x=14y. With x=125−yx=125−y, 11(125−y)=14y11(125−y)=14y gives 25y=137525y=1375, y=55y=55, and x=70x=70​. Check, 70+55=12570+55=125, and both sides of the first equation come out 4545, from 22555225​ and 18044180​. In ax+by=cax+by=c form the cleaned equation is 11x−14y=011x−14y=0, so cc is allowed to be 00.
Key idea
Cross-multiplying is still two multiplications. From pq=rsqp​=sr​, multiplying both sides by qq and then by ss gives ps=qrps=qr, which is 4.4's rule with two letters in each numerator instead of one. It applies only when each side is a single fraction and nothing else. With an extra term on either side, clear the equation by a common multiplier instead. Cleaning this shape often leaves 00 on the right, which is an ordinary ax+by=cax+by=c with c=0c=0.

Some systems are not linear in xx and yy at all. In 9x+2y=41x9​+y2​=41 the letters are in the denominators, and multiplying through by xyxy produces an xyxy term rather than a linear equation. Both equations are linear in 1xx1​ and 1yy1​ though, and those two pieces can be given names.

Problem
In 4x+3y=44x4​+y3​=44 and 7x−3y=11x7​−y3​=11, set u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​. Solve the system in uu and vv and enter uu.
Show a hint
  • Rewrite every 1xx1​ as uu and every 1yy1​ as vv, so 4xx4​ is 4u4u and 3yy3​ is 3v3v.
  • The renamed system is 4u+3v=444u+3v=44 and 7u−3v=117u−3v=11, an ordinary 5.3 problem with opposite vv-coefficients.
Show the full solution
In uu and vv the system is 4u+3v=444u+3v=44 and 7u−3v=117u−3v=11. The vv-coefficients are opposites, so adding gives 11u=5511u=55 and u=5u=5​. Then 20+3v=4420+3v=44 gives v=8v=8, and since u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​, the original values are x=15x=51​ and y=18y=81​.
Key idea
Name the repeated piece, then convert back. When both equations are linear in the same two pieces, giving those pieces names makes an ordinary system for 5.2 or 5.3. Here the pieces are 1xx1​ and 1yy1​, and elsewhere they are xx​ and yy​, or x2x2 and y2y2. Converting back undoes the naming, so u=1xu=x1​ gives x=1ux=u1​, and stopping at uu reports a different quantity, since u=5u=5 means x=15x=51​. A letter in a denominator cannot be 00, so the conversion back always works.
Problem
Solve 14x+6y=5x14​+y6​=5 and 21x−4y=1x21​−y4​=1. Neither equation has the form ax+by=cax+by=c, but naming the two repeated pieces yourself turns both into that form. Solve the renamed system and enter xx itself, not the value of the new letter.
Show a hint
  • Neither equation is linear in xx and yy, but both are linear in 1xx1​ and 1yy1​. Name those two pieces.
  • With u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​ the system is 14u+6v=514u+6v=5 and 21u−4v=121u−4v=1. Solve that by elimination, then convert with x=1ux=u1​.
Show the full solution
With u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​ the system is 14u+6v=514u+6v=5 and 21u−4v=121u−4v=1. Doubling the first and tripling the second gives 28u+12v=1028u+12v=10 and 63u−12v=363u−12v=3, and adding leaves 91u=1391u=13, so u=17u=71​ and v=12v=21​. Then x=1u=7x=u1​=7​, with y=2y=2. Check in the originals, 147+62=5714​+26​=5 and 217−42=1721​−24​=1.

Every system in this lesson was one cleanup move away from an ordinary system, and the choice between substitution and elimination came after that move rather than before it. 5.5 starts further back. The equations are not written down at all, only English sentences, and building the system is the work.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The first equation of the system 3(x+2y)=543(x+2y)=54 and x−y=6x−y=6 is not in ax+by=cax+by=c form yet. Rewrite it, solve the system, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Dividing the first equation by 33 gives x+2y=18x+2y=18. Subtracting x−y=6x−y=6 leaves 3y=123y=12, so y=4y=4. Back-substituting into x−y=6x−y=6 gives x=10x=10​. Check, 3(10+8)=543(10+8)=54 and 10−4=610−4=6. Distributing to 3x+6y=543x+6y=54 and then dividing by 33 lands on the same equation, so either route cleans it.
Practice
The system is 8x−4(y−3)=528x−4(y−3)=52 and 2x+y=342x+y=34. Clean the first equation into ax+by=cax+by=c form, then solve the system. The ask is yy, not xx.
Show the solution
Distributing gives 8x−4y+12=528x−4y+12=52, so 8x−4y=408x−4y=40 and 2x−y=102x−y=10. Adding 2x+y=342x+y=34 leaves 4x=444x=44, so x=11x=11 and y=12y=12​. Check (11,12)(11,12) in the original first equation, 88−4(9)=5288−4(9)=52. The product of −4−4 and −3−3 is +12+12, and dropping that sign change is the usual slip here.
Practice
Both sides of 9x−y=5x+3y+449x−y=5x+3y+44 carry letters. Put that equation into ax+by=cax+by=c form, solve the system it makes with 2x+5y=1202x+5y=120, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Collecting the letters on the left gives 4x−4y=444x−4y=44, and dividing by 44 leaves x−y=11x−y=11, so x=y+11x=y+11. Then 2(y+11)+5y=1202(y+11)+5y=120 collects to 7y=987y=98, so y=14y=14 and x=25x=25​. Check, 9(25)−14=2119(25)−14=211 and 5(25)+3(14)+44=2115(25)+3(14)+44=211. In x−y=11x−y=11 the letter xx has coefficient 11, so isolating it brings in no fractions.
Practice
The equation 12+3x=5y−812+3x=5y−8 is not in ax+by=cax+by=c form. Rewrite it in that form, solve it together with 2x+3y=692x+3y=69, and enter the value of yy.
Show the solution
Subtract 1212 from both sides and 5y5y from both sides to get 3x−5y=−203x−5y=−20. Multiply that by 22 for 6x−10y=−406x−10y=−40, multiply 2x+3y=692x+3y=69 by 33 for 6x+9y=2076x+9y=207, and subtract the first of those from the second for 19y=24719y=247, so y=13y=13​. Then 3x=453x=45 and x=15x=15. In the original, 12+45=5712+45=57 and 65−8=5765−8=57.
Practice
Solve x4+y5=144x​+5y​=14 and 3x−2y=363x−2y=36. Only one of the two equations has fractions to clear. Enter xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying the first equation by 2020 gives 5x+4y=2805x+4y=280. Doubling 3x−2y=363x−2y=36 gives 6x−4y=726x−4y=72, and adding leaves 11x=35211x=352, so x=32x=32​. Back-substituting gives y=30y=30. Check, 324+305=8+6=14432​+530​=8+6=14 and 96−60=3696−60=36. Only the equation with denominators needs a multiplier, and it has to reach the right side, which is why the 1414 becomes 280280.
Practice
Solve x+2y3−y4=93x+2y​−4y​=9 and 2x−y=262x−y=26. Multiply the first equation by the least common denominator to clear the fractions, then solve the cleaned system. Enter xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying the first equation by 1212 gives 4(x+2y)−3y=1084(x+2y)−3y=108, so 4x+5y=1084x+5y=108. The second equation gives y=2x−26y=2x−26, so 4x+10x−130=1084x+10x−130=108 and 14x=23814x=238, so x=17x=17​. Then y=8y=8. Check in the first equation, 17+163−84=11−2=9317+16​−48​=11−2=9. Multiply the whole numerator and not just the xx, which is why x+2yx+2y stays in parentheses until the distributing step.
Practice
Solve x2+y7=132x​+7y​=13 and x8+y5=98x​+5y​=9. The denominators differ from one equation to the other, so clear each equation with its own multiplier. Enter xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying the first equation by 1414 gives 7x+2y=1827x+2y=182, and the second by 4040 gives 5x+8y=3605x+8y=360. Four times the first is 28x+8y=72828x+8y=728, and subtracting 5x+8y=3605x+8y=360 leaves 23x=36823x=368, so x=16x=16​. Then y=35y=35. Check, 168+355=9816​+535​=9. The smallest multiplier for each equation comes from its own denominators.
Practice
Solve 0.8x+0.5y=180.8x+0.5y=18 and 0.2x−0.3y=6.20.2x−0.3y=6.2. Clear the decimals from each equation first, then eliminate. Enter yy.
Show the solution
Multiplying each equation by 1010 gives 8x+5y=1808x+5y=180 and 2x−3y=622x−3y=62. Four times the second is 8x−12y=2488x−12y=248, and subtracting that from the first leaves 17y=−6817y=−68, so y=−4y=−4​. Back-substitution gives x=25x=25. Check, 0.8(25)+0.5(−4)=20−2=180.8(25)+0.5(−4)=20−2=18 and 0.2(25)−0.3(−4)=5+1.2=6.20.2(25)−0.3(−4)=5+1.2=6.2.
Practice
Solve 0.7x+0.4y=450.7x+0.4y=45 and 0.03x+0.08y=3.50.03x+0.08y=3.5. Clear the decimals in each equation first, then solve. Enter xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying the first equation by 1010 gives 7x+4y=4507x+4y=450, and the second by 100100 gives 3x+8y=3503x+8y=350. Doubling 7x+4y=4507x+4y=450 gives 14x+8y=90014x+8y=900, and subtracting 3x+8y=3503x+8y=350 leaves 11x=55011x=550, so x=50x=50​. Then y=25y=25. Check in the second equation, 0.03(50)+0.08(25)=3.50.03(50)+0.08(25)=3.5. A multiplier of 1010 there would leave 0.3x0.3x, since a hundredths place needs a multiplier of 100100.
Practice
The system is 0.25x+0.4y=170.25x+0.4y=17 and x−y=3x−y=3. A student clears the first equation by multiplying by 100100 and writes 25x+40y=1725x+40y=17, leaving the right side alone. That line has no whole-number solution with x−y=3x−y=3 at all, which is the first sign something is wrong. Redo the clearing and enter the correct xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying every term by 100100 gives 25x+40y=170025x+40y=1700, and dividing by 55 gives 5x+8y=3405x+8y=340. With x=y+3x=y+3, 5(y+3)+8y=3405(y+3)+8y=340 gives 13y=32513y=325, so y=25y=25 and x=28x=28​. Check, 0.25(28)+0.4(25)=7+10=170.25(28)+0.4(25)=7+10=17 and 28−25=328−25=3. Multiplying only the left side changes the equation, since 25x+40y=1725x+40y=17 is the same as 0.25x+0.4y=0.170.25x+0.4y=0.17.
Practice
The system is x2−6=y82x​−6=8y​ and 2x+y=1382x+y=138. A student multiplies the first equation by 88, writes 4x−6=y4x−6=y, and reports x=24x=24. Testing (24,90)(24,90) in the first equation gives 66 on the left and 11.2511.25 on the right. Enter the correct value of xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying every term by 88 gives 4x−48=y4x−48=y, so 4x−y=484x−y=48. Adding 2x+y=1382x+y=138 gives 6x=1866x=186, so x=31x=31​. The student multiplied only the two fraction terms and left the −6−6 unchanged. With y=76y=76, the check is 15.5−6=9.515.5−6=9.5 and 768=9.5876​=9.5.
Practice
Solve 2x+y4=x+5y642x+y​=6x+5y​ and x+y=99x+y=99. Clean the first equation into ax+by=cax+by=c before using the second. Enter yy.
Show the solution
Multiplying both sides by 44 and then by 66 gives 6(2x+y)=4(x+5y)6(2x+y)=4(x+5y), so 12x+6y=4x+20y12x+6y=4x+20y and the cleaned form is 8x−14y=08x−14y=0, or 4x=7y4x=7y. With x=99−yx=99−y, 4(99−y)=7y4(99−y)=7y gives 396−4y=7y396−4y=7y, so 11y=39611y=396 and y=36y=36​. Then x=63x=63, and the original equation checks, 1624=2436=40.54162​=6243​=40.5. The fraction bar groups the whole numerator, so each numerator needs parentheses once the denominators are gone.
Practice
Solve x−y4=y6+34x−y​=6y​+3 and x+y=52x+y=52. The right side of the first equation is a fraction plus a whole number rather than a single fraction, so clear it with one multiplier instead of cross-multiplying. Enter xx.
Show the solution
Multiplying the first equation by 1212 gives 3(x−y)=2y+363(x−y)=2y+36, so 3x−5y=363x−5y=36. With x=52−yx=52−y, 3(52−y)−5y=363(52−y)−5y=36 gives 156−8y=36156−8y=36, so 8y=1208y=120, y=15y=15, and x=37x=37​. Check, 37−154=112437−15​=211​ and 156+3=112615​+3=211​. One multiplication by 1212 clears both denominators, and the 33 on the right is a term to multiply like any other.
Practice
Clean 3(x+2y)−2y=713(x+2y)−2y=71 and 8x+9y=2x+2y+1318x+9y=2x+2y+131 into ax+by=cax+by=c form. One letter's two coefficients meet at a smaller least common multiple than the other letter's, so eliminating it takes less scaling. Enter that letter.
Show the solution
Distributing gives 3x+6y−2y=713x+6y−2y=71, so 3x+4y=713x+4y=71, and collecting the second gives 6x+7y=1316x+7y=131. The xx-coefficients 33 and 66 meet at 66, which takes one scaling, while the yy-coefficients 44 and 77 meet at 2828, which takes two, so the cheaper letter is xx​. Both routes reach the same pair (9,11)(9,11), and the only difference is how large the numbers get.
Practice
In 1x+5y=33x1​+y5​=33 and 3x−1y=19x3​−y1​=19, set u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​. Solve the renamed system and enter uu.
Show the solution
Renaming gives u+5v=33u+5v=33 and 3u−v=193u−v=19. Solving the second for vv gives v=3u−19v=3u−19, so u+5(3u−19)=33u+5(3u−19)=33, which is 16u−95=3316u−95=33, then 16u=12816u=128 and u=8u=8​. Then v=5v=5, and the check gives 8+25=338+25=33 and 24−5=1924−5=19. Since u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​, the original solution is x=18x=81​ and y=15y=51​.
Practice
Solve the system 2x+3y=30x2​+y3​=30 and 5x−2y=37x5​−y2​=37. Enter xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
With u=1xu=x1​ and v=1yv=y1​ the system is 2u+3v=302u+3v=30 and 5u−2v=375u−2v=37. Doubling the first gives 4u+6v=604u+6v=60 and tripling the second gives 15u−6v=11115u−6v=111, and the sum is 19u=17119u=171, so u=9u=9 and v=4v=4. Then y=14y=41​ and x=1u=19x=u1​=91​​. The ask is xx, not uu, so 99 is one step short of the answer.
Practice
Solve x+y2+y3=232x+y​+3y​=23 and 0.15x−0.2y=1.50.15x−0.2y=1.5. Clear each equation to the form ax+by=cax+by=c first. Enter the product xyxy.
Show the solution
Multiplying the first equation by 66 gives 3(x+y)+2y=1383(x+y)+2y=138, so 3x+5y=1383x+5y=138. Multiplying the second by 100100 gives 15x−20y=15015x−20y=150, and dividing by 55 gives 3x−4y=303x−4y=30. Subtracting leaves 9y=1089y=108, so y=12y=12, and 3x=138−60=783x=138−60=78, so x=26x=26 and xy=312xy=312​. Check, 382+4=23238​+4=23 and 3.9−2.4=1.53.9−2.4=1.5. Clearing fractions and clearing decimals are the same move, one multiplier taken from the denominators and one from a power of ten.
Practice
Nonnegative numbers aa and bb satisfy a+3b=41a​+3b​=41 and a−b=13a​−b​=13. Neither equation is linear in aa and bb, but both are linear in aa​ and bb​. Name those two pieces, solve, convert back, and enter aa.
Show the solution
With u=au=a​ and v=bv=b​ the system is u+3v=41u+3v=41 and u−v=13u−v=13. Subtracting gives 4v=284v=28, so v=7v=7 and u=20u=20. Then a=u2=400a=u2=400​. Squaring is what converts back, so b=49b=49, and the check gives 20+21=4120+21=41 and 20−7=1320−7=13. Entering 2020 reports aa​ rather than aa.
Practice
Positive numbers mm and nn satisfy m2+n2=289m2+n2=289 and m2−n2=161m2−n2=161. The system is linear in m2m2 and n2n2, so name those two pieces. Enter m+nm+n.
Show the solution
With u=m2u=m2 and v=n2v=n2 the system is u+v=289u+v=289 and u−v=161u−v=161. Adding gives 2u=4502u=450, so u=225u=225 and v=64v=64. Both numbers are positive, so m=15m=15 and n=8n=8, and m+n=23m+n=23​. The naming is what makes the system linear, since m2m2 and n2n2 appear only as whole pieces.
